candidates.reason: The PR makes `scrapy check` return exit code 1 when the crawler bootstrap fails (spider could not be started). tests/test_command_check.py is the only test module that drives the check command end to end through tests.utils.cmdline.proc and asserts on its return code, so the new bootstrap-failure test and the existing exit-code assertions (test._test_contract asserting ret == 0) live here.

The PR adds a bootstrap-failure exit-code check to scrapy/commands/fetch.py, which previously always exited 0. tests/test_command_fetch.py drives `scrapy fetch` as a subprocess and is where return-code assertions for fetch (e.g. the bad-arguments usage case and the --spider path that can fail during spider loading/start) are made.

scrapy/commands/parse.py is changed to exit 1 on bootstrap errors such as a spider that cannot be found/loaded or that fails to start. tests/test_command_parse.py exercises the parse command through the CLI (including the 'Unable to find spider for' and unknown-spider paths) and is the module where the exit-code expectations are asserted.
